title: One-step switching bound for a layer-2 DNF circuit
statement:
Fix layer-2 data over $n \ge 1$ Boolean variables: a family of $N$ gates, each computing a DNF formula, with a common width bound $w \ge 1$ so that every gate has width at most $w$. Let $l \in \bbn$ and let $p \in \bbr$ satisfy $0 < p \le \tfrac{1}{40 w}$ and $p \le 1$. Consider a Bernoulli($p$) random restriction $\rho$ on the $n$ variables, in which each variable is independently left free with probability $p$ and otherwise fixed to $0$ or to $1$, each with probability $\tfrac{1-p}{2}$. Then the probability that some gate $i$ has restricted function $f_i\!\restriction_\rho$ (the gate's DNF evaluated on the free coordinates, with the fixed coordinates set by $\rho$) of decision-tree depth greater than $l$ satisfies
\[
  \bbP\!\left[\,\exists\, i:\ \mathrm{depth}\big(f_i\!\restriction_\rho\big) > l\,\right]
  \;\le\; N\left(\left(\tfrac{1}{2}\right)^{l} + \exp\!\big(-np/3\big)\right),
\]
where $\mathrm{depth}(g)$ denotes the least depth of a decision tree computing $g$.
hypotheses_covered: layer-2 data over n variables with N gates, common width bound w and w > 0
probability taken over a Bernoulli(p) random restriction
replaced:
For layer-2 data and a Bernoulli parameter $p$ with $0<p\le 1/(40\cdot\mathrm{width})$ and
$p\le 1$, the probability that some gate's restricted function has decision-tree depth greater
than $l$ is at most
\[
  \mathrm{numGates}\cdot\left((1/2)^{l} + \exp(-np/3)\right).
\]
